Definition: from G2806; a limb or shoot (as if broken off):--branch.
BiblicalUsage: Klema is a branch, a limb or shoot broken off the vine. John 15:2 says every branch in me that beareth not fruit he taketh away, and every branch that beareth fruit he purgeth, John 15:4 says the branch cannot bear fruit of itself except it abide in the vine, John 15:5 says, I am the vine, ye are the branches, and John 15:6 warns that the branch that abides not is cast forth, and withered, and cast into the fire.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe no branch has life of its own: it bears only while it abides, and it withers the hour it leaves the vine. I hold that John 15:5 is the whole Christian life in one sentence, and without me ye can do nothing is not a warning, it is a fact.
RelatedTopics: Vine and Branches; Faith; Fruit of the Spirit
